about: Judgements for fixtures/budgeted-truncation-census.json (docs/measurements/budgeted-truncation-census.md). Two independent judges per row, a third where they disagreed; every STRICT and WEAK row re-read by hand (reread_*). recall_finds are the recall probe's misses, deduplicated, with spot checks.

recall_finds.name: CappedList.init(_:limit:keeping:)
recall_finds.reason: Clamps the limit to max(0, limit), then stores Array(all.prefix(bounded)) for .leading or Array(all.suffix(bounded)) for .trailing, so the result is the longest prefix or suffix with at most limit elements. It keeps total = all.count, so wasTruncated and droppedCount report the cut exactly. Public, pure; the fixture lists only the sibling stoppedEarly at line 71.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftAssist

recall_finds.name: CIAdapter.truncateOutput(_:)
recall_finds.reason: Returns the output unchanged when count <= Self.maxErrorOutputLength (a static let of 10_000). Otherwise it returns output.prefix(10_000) followed by "\n... [truncated at 10000 chars]", so the result is not a prefix of the input. Internal method on a public actor; touches no actor state.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftAssist

recall_finds.name: IndexingHelpers.truncateOversizedChunks(_:)
recall_finds.reason: Maps over the chunks; each chunk whose content is over 4_000 Characters is rebuilt with String(content.prefix(4_000)) and its token estimate recomputed, and shorter chunks are left unchanged. So each output content is the longest Character prefix of at most 4_000. The truncation is per element, on a field, and the budget is a local literal. Internal, pure, no flag.
recall_finds.spot_check: confirmed: each chunk's content cut to a constant 4,000 characters
recall_finds.subject: SwiftAssist

recall_finds.name: ThinkingRecipeExtractor.trimStep(_:)
recall_finds.reason: Trims surrounding whitespace. If the text is over maximumStepLength (a static let of 240) it cuts at that Character offset, trims trailing whitespace and appends "…". Private static, pure.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftAssist

recall_finds.name: ThinkingRecipeExtractor.deriveName(from:)
recall_finds.reason: Takes the first step, trimmed; returns "Extracted Recipe" when steps is empty. If that step is over maximumNameLength (a static let of 60) it returns the first 60 Characters, trailing whitespace trimmed, plus "…". It truncates steps[0], not the input array. Internal static, pure.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftAssist

recall_finds.name: ChatViewModel.generateTitle()
recall_finds.reason: Takes no parameters. It reads the first user message from self.messages ("New Chat" if there is none), takes prefix(50), and appends "…" when anything was cut. The budget is also the literal 50. Private, reads view-model state, so not pure.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftAssist

recall_finds.name: MLXValidateCommand.preview(_:)
recall_finds.reason: First replaces newlines with spaces. If the result is over 80 Characters it returns prefix(80) + "…", otherwise the one-line text. Internal, pure; the budget is the literal 80.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftAssist

recall_finds.name: InsecureTransportVisitor.truncateURL(_:)
recall_finds.reason: If urlString.count > 60 it returns String(urlString.prefix(57)) + "...", so the result is exactly 60 Characters; otherwise it returns the input unchanged. The budget is the literals 60 and 57, so the census found no integer parameter.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftProjectLint

recall_finds.name: ViolationFormatter.nearMissLines(_:)
recall_finds.reason: It caps the near-miss list at a local constant `let cap = 5` using nearMisses.prefix(cap). It formats each entry as a bullet under a 'Near-misses (N):' header and appends '… N more' when entries were dropped. It returns nil for nil input and a 'none.' line for empty input. There is no integer parameter, so the census never saw a budget.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftPropertyLaws

recall_finds.name: manualCollect(from:cap:)
recall_finds.reason: Calls iterator.next() and appends while pulled < cap, so it returns the first min(cap, n) elements of the sequence. A zero or negative cap returns []. It is private, and the census missed it because the input's type is a generic S: Sequence, which its type regex does not recognise.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftPropertyLaws

recall_finds.name: snapshot(_:)
recall_finds.reason: The body is "\(Array(sample.prefix(8)))…": it renders the first 8 elements and always appends '…', even when nothing was dropped. It is private. The budget is the literal 8, so there is no budget parameter, and the input C: Collection is also outside the census shape.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftPropertyLaws

recall_finds.name: collect(_:cap:)
recall_finds.reason: Same body as manualCollect: a while pulled < cap, let element = iterator.next() loop, which returns the longest prefix of at most cap elements. It is private, and the input is a generic S: Sequence that the census does not see as a sequence.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftPropertyLaws

recall_finds.name: ActivityGraphBuilder.compactText(_:)
recall_finds.reason: Trims the text, turns newlines into spaces and collapses runs of whitespace. Then, if the result is over 80 Characters, it returns prefix(77) + "…". Because of the normalization the result is not a prefix of the raw input even before the marker. Internal static, pure.
recall_finds.subject: SwiftUMLStudio

recall_finds.name: Cursor.prefix(_:)
recall_finds.reason: Returns PrefixCursor(self, maxLength:), whose next() returns nil once taken >= maxLength and otherwise passes through base.next(). That gives the first min(maxLength, n) elements, and a zero or negative budget gives an empty cursor. The census missed it because PrefixCursor<Self> is not a sequence result in its shape, and it does not count a Cursor owner as sequence input either.
recall_finds.spot_check: confirmed: element-count prefix, on GRDB's lazy Cursor rather than a drawable input
recall_finds.subject: grdb

recall_finds.name: Cursor.suffix(_:)
recall_finds.reason: Drains the cursor into a ring buffer of size maxLength, then rotates it, so it returns the last min(maxLength, n) elements in order. maxLength 0 returns [] and a negative maxLength trips GRDBPrecondition. The result [Element] fits the census shape, but the input is self, a Cursor, which the census does not count as a sequence (the call also consumes the cursor).
recall_finds.subject: grdb

recall_finds.name: BigString._Chunk._succinctContents(maxLength:)
recall_finds.reason: It appends about maxLength leading escaped characters of the chunk via _appendQuotedProtectingLeft(maxLength: c). When more remains it inserts "..." and then the last c characters, and the whole thing is wrapped in prefix/suffix counts (description calls it with the constant 10). The budget is an Int and the result is a String, but the owner _Chunk is not a recognised sequence type and no parameter is a sequence.
recall_finds.subject: swift-collections

recall_finds.name: PathComponentScanner.scan(length:)
recall_finds.reason: Body is `defer { remaining = remaining.dropFirst(length) }; return remaining.prefix(length)`, so it returns the longest prefix of at most `length` Characters of the scanner's stored `remaining` Substring, or all of it when shorter. PREFIX, FITS and MAXIMAL hold; a negative length traps in prefix/dropFirst. The instrument missed it because the sequence it truncates is a stored property of a non-sequence scanner struct, not a parameter or a sequence `self` (compare swift-system `_eat(count:)`, which is in the fixture). It is a private mutating tokenizer consumer (pure: no, no flag).
recall_finds.subject: swift-docc

recall_finds.name: StringScanner.take(_:)
recall_finds.reason: Same body as PathComponentScanner.scan(length:): it returns `remaining.prefix(count)` and advances `remaining` by `dropFirst(count)`. The result is the longest prefix of at most `count` Characters of the stored Substring, or all of it when shorter, and a negative count traps. The input is a stored property of the `private struct StringScanner`, not a parameter, so the instrument missed it. Effectively fileprivate, mutating (pure: no), no flag.
recall_finds.subject: swift-docc

recall_finds.name: NodeURLGenerator.fileSafeURL(_:)
recall_finds.reason: Borderline sanitizer. For each URL path component with count >= 240 it returns `String(name.prefix(240)).appendingHashedIdentifier(name)` (a '-<hash>' marker), and if the joined path's count >= 880 it does the same with prefix(880) plus a hash. It also prepends "'" to components that start with '.'. The budgets are fileprivate constants and the input and result are a URL, not a sequence, so the instrument could not see it. The result is not a prefix (marker, possible "'") and exceeds the budget by the hash length. public static, pure (deterministic stableHashString), no flag.
recall_finds.subject: swift-docc

recall_finds.name: Platform.copyCString(dst:src:size:)
recall_finds.reason: A strlcpy wrapper. On Darwin it calls strlcpy; elsewhere it copies src into a size-byte buffer and NUL-terminates when truncated. Either way dst ends up holding the longest byte prefix of src that fits size-1 bytes, and the return value srcLen acts as the truncation flag. Caveats: it may split a multi-byte UTF-8 character, and on the non-Darwin path size <= 0 traps. The census missed it because the result goes through the dst pointer and the function returns Int.
recall_finds.spot_check: re-classified OTHER: an strlcpy-style copy through unsafe pointers that returns the source length and cuts on bytes, not characters
recall_finds.subject: swift-foundation

rows.reason: When count < newLength it left-pads with padString (precondition: one character) up to newLength, so the result is longer than the input and not a suffix of it. Otherwise it returns the last newLength characters, which is a strict longest-suffix truncation on that branch only. A negative newLength traps because the index offset runs past endIndex.
Returns a copy of the request with relation.limit = SQLLimit(limit:offset:), replacing any earlier limit. It configures a capped (and optionally offset) database fetch and truncates no input.

wrapped(to:wrappingIndent:) word-wraps the whole string. It repeatedly takes a prefix(columns) chunk, cuts at the last newline or space, indents each non-empty line and joins with "\n", so no text is dropped and a word longer than the width overflows. When columns - wrappingIndent <= 0 it asserts in debug and returns "".

BitSet.random(upTo:) only calls the rng overload with a SystemRandomNumberGenerator. That overload builds a random BitSet whose members lie in 0..<limit, so limit bounds the member values, not the size of an input. No input is truncated.

It traps if limit < 0 and returns an empty set for 0. Otherwise it fills words with rng.next() and masks the last word with _Word(upTo: b), producing a random set of integers below limit. This is random generation, not truncation of an input.
BitSet.Counted.random(upTo:) wraps BitSet.random(upTo:) in BitSet.Counted. It generates a random set of members below limit and truncates no input.
It wraps BitSet.random(upTo:using:) in BitSet.Counted, producing a random set bounded by limit from the inout rng. This is random generation, not budgeted truncation.

A consuming iterator step. It returns the sub-span [index, end), where end = index + min(maxCount, count - index), clipped to limit when index <= limit < end, then sets the inout index to end. It traps unless maxCount > 0 and index and limit are in bounds. The slice starts at an arbitrary offset, so it is not a prefix of the input.

The same logic as _nextMutableSpan, but as a mutating borrow. It extracts [index, min(index+maxCount, count, limit-if-ahead)) and advances the inout index. This is a chunked iteration step starting at an offset, not prefix truncation.

It only calls Span._nextSpan(after:maxCount:limitedBy:), which returns the slice [index, end) with end capped by maxCount, count and limit, and advances the inout index to end. The slice starts at an offset, so it is an iteration chunk, not a prefix.

prefix(n) returns self when n >= count. Otherwise it returns the first n elements across the two segments: first._extracting(first: n), or first plus second._extracting(first: n - first.count). That is exactly the longest prefix of at most n elements, including n = 0. A negative n asserts in debug and hits _extracting's precondition in release.
rows.reread_note: element-count prefix of a deque's unsafe segment pair; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: suffix(n) returns self when n >= count. Otherwise it returns the last n elements: from first when there is no second segment, from second when n <= second.count, or first._extracting(last: n - second.count) plus second. That is exactly the longest suffix of at most n elements. A negative n traps (assert, or _extracting's precondition).
rows.reread_note: element-count suffix of a deque's unsafe segment pair; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: Storage.allocate(byteCapacity:) heap-allocates node storage. It rounds byteCapacity up to a power-of-two number of units plus alignment slack and asserts that the capacity it gets is >= byteCapacity. The budget is a minimum to round up to, not a cap.

_HashNode.allocate allocates storage sized for the items and children plus extraBytes of free space, sets the bitmaps and bytesFree, and runs the caller's initializer on the child and item buffers. It is a node constructor; nothing is truncated.

allocateCollision asserts count >= 2, allocates count * stride + hash bytes + extraBytes, stores the hash and runs the initializer on the item buffer. It allocates and initializes a collision node; nothing is truncated.

mapValuesToVoid converts the node to Value == Void, by unsafeBitCast when Value is already Void and by mapValues otherwise. It copies the node when copy is set or when it lacks extraBytes of free space. extraBytes is the minimum free space to reserve, not a cap. No input is truncated.

_nextSpan traps unless maxCount > 0 and index and limit are in [0, count]. It returns extracting(index..<end), where end = index + min(maxCount, count - index), lowered to limit when index <= limit < end, and writes end back to the inout index. It is a chunk starting at an arbitrary offset, not a prefix of the span.

_trim(first:) traps if maxLength < 0, returns an empty span for a cut of 0, and otherwise returns extracting(first: min(maxLength, count)), the longest prefix of at most maxLength elements. It is mutating: the returned prefix is also dropped from self.
rows.reread_note: mutating _trim(first:) on Span returns the cut prefix; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: _trim(last:) traps if maxLength < 0, returns an empty span for a cut of 0, and otherwise returns extracting(last: min(maxLength, count)), the longest suffix of at most maxLength elements. It is mutating: the returned suffix is also dropped from self.
rows.reread_note: mutating _trim(last:) on Span returns the cut suffix; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: Returns self unchanged when count >= width; otherwise prepends (width - count) copies of `character`. It only ever lengthens the string to the width and never truncates, so this is left-padding.
Returns self unchanged when count >= width; otherwise appends (width - count) copies of `character`. This is right-padding. It never shortens the input.

Returns self unchanged when count >= width; otherwise puts ceil((width-count)/2) pad characters before it and floor((width-count)/2) after. This is centering padding, and a longer input is never truncated.

Returns Self(start: baseAddress, count: min(maxLength, count)), which is exactly the first min(maxLength, count) elements. That is the longest element prefix within the budget, including budget 0 and an input shorter than the budget. A negative maxLength traps on a precondition rather than violating a law.
rows.reread_note: _extracting(first:) = min(maxLength, count) elements; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: Advances the base by cut = min(maxLength, count) and returns the remaining count - cut elements, so this is dropFirst. The budget is the number of elements to drop, not a bound on the result's size, so FITS does not hold.

Computes newCount = min(maxLength, count) and returns extracting(count - newCount ..< count), which is exactly the last min(maxLength, count) elements. That is the longest suffix fitting the element budget. A negative budget traps on a precondition.
rows.reread_note: _extracting(last:) = min(maxLength, count) elements; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: Returns Self(start: baseAddress, count: count - min(maxLength, count)), so this is dropLast. The result is a prefix, but the budget counts elements dropped and does not bound the result's size, so FITS and MAXIMAL do not apply.

With cut = min(maxLength, count), it returns the first `cut` elements (an empty nil-based buffer when cut == 0) and mutates self to the remaining count - cut elements. The returned value is the longest element prefix within the budget. It is not pure because it mutates the receiver, and a negative budget traps on a precondition.
rows.reread_note: mutating _trim(first:) on UnsafeBufferPointer; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: With cut = min(maxLength, count), it returns the last `cut` elements (start + count - cut, an empty buffer when cut == 0) and shrinks self to the leading count - cut. The returned value is the longest element suffix within the budget. It mutates the receiver, and a negative budget traps.
rows.reread_note: mutating _trim(last:) on UnsafeBufferPointer; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: Same body as the UnsafeBufferPointer version: it returns Self(start: baseAddress, count: min(maxLength, count)), the longest element prefix within the budget. A negative maxLength traps on a precondition.
rows.reread_note: _extracting(first:) on UnsafeMutableBufferPointer; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: Advances by min(maxLength, count) and returns the remaining elements, so this is dropFirst. The budget is a drop count, not a bound on the result's size.

Returns extracting(count - newCount ..< count) with newCount = min(maxLength, count), which is the last min(maxLength, count) elements and the longest suffix within the budget. A negative budget traps on a precondition.
rows.reread_note: _extracting(last:) on UnsafeMutableBufferPointer; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: Returns the first count - min(maxLength, count) elements, so this is dropLast. The budget is the number of trailing elements to drop and does not bound the result's size.

Returns the first cut = min(maxLength, count) elements (an empty buffer when cut == 0) and mutates self to the rest. The return value is the longest element prefix fitting the budget. It mutates the receiver, and a negative budget traps.
rows.reread_note: mutating _trim(first:) on UnsafeMutableBufferPointer; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: Returns the last cut = min(maxLength, count) elements and shrinks self to the leading count - cut. The return value is the longest element suffix within the budget. It mutates the receiver, and a negative budget traps.
rows.reread_note: mutating _trim(last:) on UnsafeMutableBufferPointer; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: This is a local function nested inside BucketIterator.description, so its effective visibility is private. It returns s unchanged when s.count >= length and otherwise prepends (length - count) padding characters. It is left-padding and never truncates.

With c = min(n, count), it returns a new InputSpan over the first c initialized elements (slot 0 of the initialized region) and decrements self._count by c, which removes them from the receiver. The returned span is the longest element prefix within the budget. It mutates and transfers ownership, and a negative n traps on a precondition.
rows.reread_note: consumePrefix(upTo:) on InputSpan; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: It delegates to readBytesFromFile, which does file I/O and reads min(st_size, maxLength ?? Int.max) raw bytes. The capped thing is the file's contents, not an input sequence. It throws for a negative maxLength (ENOMEM), and on Linux a file reporting size 0 is read in full regardless of maxLength.

Returns the 256-bit full-width product self * 10^exponent as a (high, low) pair, with a UInt64 fast path when exponent <= 19. This is pure arithmetic with no truncation of a sequence, and it traps if exponent is outside the pow10 table.

This static helper divides a 256-bit (high, low) dividend by 10^exponent using short division (two rounds when exponent > 19) and returns the quotient and remainder. It is arithmetic, and the exponent is a power of ten, not a budget.

Builds a Decimal from a 256-bit significand and tail by dividing it down to fit 128 bits and minExponent, rounding with sticky/round digits, then regrowing toward maxExponent. It returns (result, inexact) and throws .underflow or .overflow. This is numeric rounding, not prefix truncation; the inexact flag reports precision loss.

Returns BufferView(start: start, count: min(maxLength, count)), the first min(maxLength, count) elements and so the longest element prefix within the budget. A negative maxLength traps on a precondition. BufferView is an internal struct.
rows.reread_note: BufferView.prefix(_:) in FoundationEssentials' JSON decoder; its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: Computes nc = min(maxLength, count) and returns a view starting at start + (count - nc) with nc elements, which is exactly the longest element suffix within the budget. A negative maxLength traps on a precondition.
rows.reread_note: BufferView.suffix(_:); its input is an unsafe buffer, span or buffer view; no generator draws one

rows.reason: Returns the raw-byte window byteOffset ..< byteOffset + byteSize when byteSize <= 8. Otherwise it returns only the last 8 bytes of that window, the significant bytes of an oversized bplist integer. It slices at a caller-given offset, and the bounds are only asserted, not clamped.

It copies exactly `length` bytes from a C file-system path into a temporary buffer. finalPathLength then appends a trailing '/' (directory) or strips trailing slashes, and the result is parsed into a _URLInfo; `length <= 0` yields "./". `length` is the size of the source buffer, not a budget. resolveBaseURL can read the current directory, so the function is not pure.

rangeWithinReadableBytes accepts only index >= readerIndex, length >= 0 and index+length within the readable bytes. In that case it returns exactly `length` bytes starting at offset `index`; in every other case it returns nil. It never shortens the result to fit.

It calls getBytes(at: readerIndex, length:). When at least `length` bytes are readable it returns exactly that many leading readable bytes and advances the reader index (mutating). When fewer are readable or length < 0 it returns nil and does not truncate.

It is getBytes(at: readerIndex, length:) and does not move the reader index. It returns exactly `length` leading readable bytes, or nil when fewer are readable or length < 0, never a shortened prefix.

It decodes exactly `length` bytes at offset `index` with String(decoding:as: UTF8), which repairs invalid sequences with U+FFFD and can split a scalar at the end. It returns nil when the range is not fully readable or length < 0, and never truncates to fit.

It calls getString(at: readerIndex, length:): it decodes exactly `length` leading readable bytes (lossy UTF-8 repair) and advances the reader index (mutating). It returns nil when fewer than `length` bytes are readable, with no truncation.
It is getString(at: readerIndex, length:) and does not move the reader index. It returns the lossy UTF-8 decode of exactly `length` leading readable bytes, or nil when not enough bytes are readable.

It calls getSlice_inlineAlways(at: readerIndex, length:). It returns a buffer of exactly `length` leading readable bytes and advances the reader index (mutating), or nil if length < 0 or the range passes writerIndex. It never truncates.

It takes getSlice(at: index, length:) and returns nil when that range is not readable. It throws ReadUTF8ValidationError.invalidUTF8 when the exact `length` bytes are not valid UTF-8, and otherwise returns them decoded. It does not truncate to a budget.

It calls getUTF8ValidatedString(at: readerIndex, length:): nil when fewer than `length` bytes are readable, a throw on invalid UTF-8. On success it returns exactly `length` leading bytes as a String and advances the reader index (mutating).

It is getUTF8ValidatedString(at: readerIndex, length:) without moving the reader index. It returns exactly `length` leading readable bytes decoded, nil when not enough are readable, or throws on invalid UTF-8.

It delegates to getSlice_inlineAlways. That returns a ByteBuffer viewing exactly bytes index..<index+length (readerIndex 0, writerIndex length), copying when the slice start passes 16 MiB. It returns nil when index < readerIndex, length < 0 or the range passes writerIndex, and never shortens to fit.

A guard requires index >= 0, length >= 0, index >= readerIndex and index + length <= writerIndex, else nil. It then rebuilds _slice as sliceStart..<sliceStart+length, or copies via the slow path, and sets reader/writer indices to 0/length. The result is an exact-length slice at an offset, not a truncation.
It is getSlice(at: readerIndex, length:). It returns a buffer of exactly `length` leading readable bytes, or nil when fewer are readable or length < 0, never a shortened slice.
A static factory that wraps the argument as HexDumpFormat(.plain(maxBytes: maxBytes)). It builds a configuration value and truncates nothing; the clipping happens later in _hexDump(maxBytes:).
A static factory that returns HexDumpFormat(.detailed(maxBytes: maxBytes)). It is a configuration value with no input sequence and no truncation.
A static factory that returns HexDumpFormat(.compact(maxBytes: maxBytes)). It is a configuration value with no input sequence and no truncation.

If readableBytes <= maxBytes it returns the full hex dump. Otherwise it returns the hex of the first maxBytes/2 bytes, then " ... " (or "..."), then the hex of the last maxBytes/2 bytes. That is a head+tail elision with a marker, not a prefix: an odd maxBytes shows maxBytes-1 bytes, and maxBytes <= -2 crashes on the force-unwrapped readSlice of a negative length.

It delegates to _hexDump(maxBytes:separateWithWhitespace: true). It gives the full space-separated hex when it fits, otherwise the first maxBytes/2 and last maxBytes/2 bytes joined by " ... ", so the marker sits in the middle and the result is not a prefix.

This delegates to _hexDump(maxBytes:separateWithWhitespace:false). If readableBytes <= maxBytes it hex-encodes the whole buffer. Otherwise it hex-encodes the first maxBytes/2 bytes and the last maxBytes/2 bytes, joined by "...". The result is a head-plus-tail selection rendered as hex, not a prefix with a marker appended, so it is OTHER. The "..." is an in-band flag that can't be confused with output, because hex output only uses 0-9a-f. An odd maxBytes shows only maxBytes-1 bytes, and maxBytes <= -2 traps because readSlice returns nil for a negative length and the result is force-unwrapped.

Formats one hexdump -C line: an 8-digit hex lineOffset, the slice's bytes split into an 8-byte left column (prefix(8 - paddingBefore)) and the rest, space-padded to 60 columns, then an ASCII column padded by paddingBefore/paddingAfter. Nothing is truncated to a budget; the integer parameters are an offset label and padding widths.

If readableBytes <= maxBytes it returns the full hexdump -C style dump. Otherwise it dumps the first maxBytes/2 bytes, a fixed dotted separator line, the last maxBytes/2 bytes (offsets taken from writerIndex), and always a final length line. That is a head-plus-tail selection of a formatted rendering, not a prefix of the input. The separator line is an in-band truncation flag. maxBytes <= -2 traps because readSlice returns nil for a negative length and the result is force-unwrapped.

Reads an Integer length prefix at `index` and returns getSlice(at: index + MemoryLayout<Integer>.size, length: prefix). The length comes from the buffer's own data, not a caller budget. It returns nil when the prefix can't be read, is negative or isn't exactly representable as Int, or when too few bytes follow, rather than truncating.

Arena allocator: allocates tailOffset + stride(Fields) + trailingByteCount bytes in the arena, initializes the header and fields, and returns the node plus a pointer to the trailing region. trailingByteCount is an extra-allocation size, not a budget that truncates an input.

Token constructor: it views wholeTextLength bytes of sourceBuffer and computes the text range from leadingTriviaByteLength/textByteLength. It then allocates (copying the text) either a smol or a full parsed-token node into the arena. The integers describe token geometry, and nothing is truncated.

Token constructor: it interns the text in the arena unless it is the kind's static default text, then packs kind/text/trivia/numLeadingTrivia/byteLength into a MaterializedToken payload and allocates a node. byteLength and numLeadingTrivia are stored metadata, not truncation budgets.

Layout-node constructor: it validates the layout for the kind, packs layout/byteLength/descendantCount/recursiveFlags into a Layout payload, and allocates it in the arena. The integers are precomputed metadata stored as given, not budgets.

Allocates an arena buffer of `count` child slots and runs the caller's initializer on it. It then sums the children's byteLength/totalNodes, merges flags (adding hasMaximumNestingLevelOverflow if requested), registers the children with the arena, and builds a layout node. count sizes an allocation and nothing is truncated. It is public under @_spi(RawSyntax).

BSP clipping: it walks the tree from nodes[0], splitting the polygons along each node plane and collecting the front or back fragments (merging fragments that share an id) according to the ClipRule. It mutates the inout `out` and the inout id counter, and returns [] on cancellation. `id` is a fragment-id counter, not a budget.

Builds an NSAttributedString from text/font/color and delegates to Path.text(_: NSAttributedString), which lays out the glyphs via CoreText (line-wrapping at the optional width) and turns each CGPath into a Path. `detail` is the curve-approximation resolution, so this renders glyphs rather than truncating anything.

Wraps Path.text(String, font:width:detail:) in Self(...), returning the glyph-contour paths of the laid-out text. `detail` sets curve approximation and `width` sets line-wrapping width; nothing is truncated.
Wraps Path.text(NSAttributedString, width:detail:) in Self(...): glyph contours from CoreText layout with optional line wrap. `detail` is curve resolution, not a truncation budget.
Returns Path.text(String, font:width:detail:) unchanged as [Path]: the glyph contours of rendered text. `detail` is curve approximation, and nothing is cut to a budget.
Returns Path.text(NSAttributedString, width:detail:) unchanged: the glyph contours of laid-out attributed text. `detail` is curve resolution, not a budget.

Builds an NSAttributedString and delegates to Mesh.text(NSAttributedString,...), which extrudes each glyph CGPath (approximated at `detail`) to `depth`, caches repeated glyphs, translates them, and unions the meshes. It is geometry generation, not truncation.

For each CoreText glyph path it builds a Path at `detail`, extrudes it to `depth` (cached per CGPath), translates it to the glyph position, and returns the union, or .empty if cancelled. `detail` is curve resolution, not a size budget.

Picks a cross-section from `detail`: a line for detail 1 or 2, otherwise a circle with `detail` segments. It extrudes that along the shape with the miter limit and returns the resulting mesh. `detail` sets cross-section sides, so nothing is truncated.

Strokes each path in the collection with the single-path stroke(width:miterLimit:detail:) and returns the union of the resulting meshes. It is geometry generation with `detail` as cross-section sides, not truncation.

Makes a circle cross-section with max(3, detail) segments. For each line segment it rotates and translates the circle to both endpoints and lofts between them into a polygon list, stopping early if cancelled, and returns one mesh. `detail` is a resolution clamped up to 3, not a budget.

Revolves a profile into a mesh: it returns .empty for fewer than 2 points, clamps slices to at least 3, optionally subdivides edges near the poles poleDetail times, and emits triangles/quads for each slice. The 'break' only exits on isCancelled(); slices and poleDetail are resolution parameters, not truncation budgets.

Delegates to [Polygon].tessellate(maxSides:), which leaves each convex polygon with <= max(maxSides, 3) vertices as is. Otherwise it triangulates the polygon and re-merges the pieces into convex polygons of at most maxSides sides. It splits polygons rather than truncating an input, then rebuilds the Mesh, dropping cached bounds/convexity if cancelled.

Generates a closed elliptical Path of curve points sampled at angle steps of 2π/max(3, segments), with radii clamped to at least scaleLimit/2. segments is a sampling resolution, so this generates points and truncates nothing.

Generates a new closed rounded-rectangle Path from width/height/radius; `detail` is the number of arc segments emitted per corner (stride step pi/(2*detail)), and detail <= 0 or a tiny radius falls back to a plain rectangle. There is no input sequence to truncate, so the budget sets output resolution, not a cut.

Builds a quadratic-Bezier path from the control points, inserting `detail` interpolated points per curved section via `arc(...)`; detail <= 0 or fewer than 3 points returns the sanitized points unchanged. The output is a superset (interpolation) of the input, not a prefix, and `detail` is a resolution, not a size budget.

Recursively subdivides segments, inserting a curved midpoint wherever a segment's share of the twist reaches 2pi/(detail/2), until no segment does; detail <= 2 or zero twist returns self. It adds points rather than dropping any, so the result is never a truncated prefix.

flatMaps Polygon.tessellate(maxSides:), which keeps convex polygons with <= max(maxSides,3) vertices and otherwise triangulates and re-merges them into convex pieces of at most maxSides sides. It decomposes each polygon into bounded pieces rather than keeping a prefix. Behaviour also depends on the caller's isCancelled callback.

Groups polygons by material and plane, then merges coplanar neighbours via coplanarDetessellate, with each merged polygon capped at maxSides vertices; it returns [] (or a partial batch) when isCancelled fires, and runs the groups through `batch`. This is a geometric merge whose output is not a prefix of the input.

Repeatedly replaces polygon i with a merged polygon and removes j (bestMergeCandidate or greedyDetessellate), where maxSides limits each merged polygon's vertex count; it returns [] when cancelled. The result is a merged polygon set, not a truncated prefix of the input.

Applies round(smoothing*3) passes of a 1/4-1/2-1/4 neighbour average to the points, then delegates to resample(distance:maximumPointCount:), which emits new evenly spaced interpolated points. The output is a smoothed, resampled polyline, not a prefix of the input; <= 1 point returns the input unchanged.

Walks the polyline and emits new points interpolated at a uniform targetDistance; with maximumPointCount it widens the spacing to totalLength/(max-2) and stops appending once the count reaches max-1, then appends the endpoint if room remains. The result is generated interpolated geometry spanning the whole stroke, not a prefix (and for max <= 0 it still returns one point).

Splits the array into consecutive slices of maximumCount elements (the last may be shorter) using stride(from:0,to:count,by:maximumCount), and returns [] when maximumCount <= 0 or the array is empty. The output is a list of chunks covering every element; nothing is dropped.

Resamples the mask texture on the GPU (HarbethIO with a MaskCoverageResample filter) to max(width,1) x max(height,1), scaling the affine transform to match, and returns self when the dimensions and sampling are unchanged. It is image scaling with Metal I/O, and it throws on failure.

Rounds packedBytesPerRow up to the MTLDevice's texture-buffer alignment, then copies each source row into a zero-filled buffer at the wider stride. It returns (paddedBytes, alignedRowBytes), or the input unchanged when the stride is already aligned. This is row padding that depends on a device query, not truncation.
Computes an FNV-1a 64-bit hash over `data` and returns the string "cube|dimension|min|max|hexhash". `dimension` is only interpolated into the string; nothing is truncated.

Builds a rows x columns grid of normalized control points (column/(columns-1), row/(rows-1)). It throws if either dimension is < 2, if the product overflows, or if it exceeds maximumControlPointCount. It is a constructor with no input sequence to truncate.

Factory that packs its arguments into a CoreContext and a StringContext(maxLength:minLength:pattern:...) and returns .string(core, string). minLength/maxLength are stored as schema metadata and nothing is truncated.

Variadic-allowedValues overload that forwards every argument to the array-allowedValues .string(...) factory, which stores minLength/maxLength in a StringContext. It builds a schema value and truncates nothing.

Factory that builds a CoreContext and an IntegerContext(multipleOf:maximum:minimum:) and returns .integer(core, integer). multipleOf/maximum are stored schema constraints with no truncation behaviour.

Variadic-allowedValues overload that forwards all arguments to the array-allowedValues .integer(...) factory, which stores multipleOf/maximum/minimum in an IntegerContext. It is a schema constructor and truncates nothing.

Factory that builds a CoreContext and an ObjectContext(properties:patternProperties:additionalProperties:maxProperties:minProperties:) and returns .object(...). The property dictionaries are stored whole and min/maxProperties are only metadata, so nothing is capped.

Factory that builds a CoreContext and an ArrayContext(items:maxItems:minItems:prefixItems:uniqueItems:) and returns .array(...). maxItems is stored as a schema constraint and prefixItems is stored whole, so no truncation happens.

OpenAPI 3.0 factory that packs its arguments into a CoreContext and a StringContext(maxLength:minLength:pattern:) and returns .string(...). The length bounds are stored metadata and nothing is truncated.
Variadic-allowedValues overload that forwards every argument to the array-allowedValues .string(...) factory. It is a schema constructor and truncates nothing.

OpenAPI 3.0 factory that builds a CoreContext and an IntegerContext(multipleOf:maximum:minimum:), whose init just stores them, and returns .integer(...). These are stored numeric constraints, not a truncation budget.
Variadic-allowedValues overload that forwards all arguments to the array-allowedValues .integer(...) factory. It is a schema constructor and truncates nothing.

OpenAPI 3.0 factory that builds a CoreContext and an ObjectContext(properties:additionalProperties:maxProperties:minProperties:), whose init stores the values, and returns .object(...). The properties are kept whole and maxProperties is only metadata.

A factory that packs its arguments into a CoreContext and an ArrayContext(items:maxItems:minItems:uniqueItems:) and returns .array(core, arrayContext). maxItems/minItems are stored as schema constraints. Nothing is truncated.

Builds a GET /api/v4/Battery/cycles request, adding `limit` as a query item, runs it over the network and returns the decoded body. Any capping of the list happens on the server, applied to fetched data rather than to an input sequence.

Fills a buffer with the first `count` elements and sorts it, then scans the rest of the sequence, inserting each element >= result[0] and shifting out the smallest. It returns the `count` largest elements in ascending order, a selection rather than a prefix. With count 0 and a non-empty sequence it would index result[0] on an empty array, so it relies on the caller to guard that case.

Sequence.max(count:sortedBy:) traps (precondition) on a negative count, returns [] for 0, and otherwise calls _maxImplementation. That helper keeps a sorted reservoir of the count largest elements, so it returns the top-k elements in sorted order, not a contiguous prefix or suffix of the input.
This only calls max(count:sortedBy: <) on Sequence, which selects the count largest elements and returns them sorted ascending. The result is a top-k selection, not a prefix or suffix of the input.

Collection.min(count:sortedBy:) clamps count to self.count, traps on a negative count, and returns either sorted(by:).prefix(k) or _minImplementation's sorted reservoir. Either way the result is the k smallest elements in sorted order. It is a prefix of a sorted copy, not of the input.

Collection.max(count:sortedBy:) clamps count to self.count, traps if it is negative, and returns sorted(by:).suffix(k) or _maxImplementation's top-k reservoir. The result is the k largest elements, a suffix of the sorted copy, not of the input.

This only calls Collection.max(count:sortedBy: <), which returns the k largest elements sorted, via sorted().suffix(k) or a partial-sort reservoir. It is a top-k selection, not a contiguous piece of the input.

Collection.randomSample returns [] for k <= 0. Otherwise it fills a reservoir with the first k elements, replaces some at random offsets drawn from the inout rng (Algorithm L), and shuffles the result. It is a random subset in random order, and it consumes RNG state.

Sequence.randomSample is the same reservoir sampling over an iterator. The `break` ends the loop when the iterator runs out, not when a budget is hit. It returns a shuffled random subset of up to k elements, not a prefix.
Returns Attribute(name: "cols", value: width.description). It only turns the integer into an HTML attribute string. No input is truncated.
Clamps offset to [0, 8] with Swift.min(8, Swift.max(0, offset)) and returns it as the "headingoffset" attribute value. This is a numeric clamp, not truncation of a sequence.
Returns Attribute(name: "max", value: value.description), which just stores an integer as an HTML attribute. Nothing is truncated.
Returns Attribute(name: "maxlength", value: value.description). It only declares a maximum-length attribute and never truncates text.
Returns Attribute(name: "minlength", value: value.description), an integer turned into an attribute string. No truncation.
Returns Attribute(name: "size", value: width.description), an integer turned into an attribute string. No truncation.
Returns Attribute(name: "width", value: pixels.description), an integer turned into an attribute string. No truncation.

Returns "" for an empty list and the single element for a one-item list. Otherwise it pads (or, via NSString padding, cuts) every column but the last to the static briefSummaryColumnWidth (15), joins them with " | ", then appends the separator and the last column. The `length` parameter is never read, and the result is a joined, padded row, not a prefix of the input. It reads a private static var that is never mutated, so it is pure in practice.

Returns sourceLine unchanged when highlighting is off or the line is outside the range. A multi-line range wraps the whole line in ANSI codes. Otherwise it splits the line's UTF-8 view at the column offsets into before/highlighted/after and puts ANSI highlight codes around the middle part, so the output is the full line with escape codes inserted, not a truncated prefix.
Builds and returns SourceLocation(line: 0, column: startColumn) ..< SourceLocation(line: 0, column: endColumn). It is a range constructor with no input sequence.
Calls makeRelativeRange(startColumn:endColumn: startColumn + length) and returns that range. Computing the end column by addition is the only logic.

Returns the whole of rawPath when trailingComponentsToDrop <= 0. Otherwise it splits the path into components, drops (n-1) from the end, and returns rawPath up to the start of the last remaining component, i.e. the path with its last n components removed but the trailing separator kept, or "" when n is at least the component count. The result is a prefix, but the integer is a count of components to drop (dropLast), not a size budget the result must fit, so FITS and MAXIMAL don't apply.

Returns self.prefix(c), the first min(c, count) elements: the longest element prefix within c (an empty slice for c == 0, the whole slice when shorter). It then mutates self to dropFirst(c). A negative c traps on prefix's precondition instead of truncating. It is a mutating parser consumer, so not pure, and it returns no flag.
rows.reread_note: internal mutating Slice._eat(count:) returns prefix(c) and drops it; a Slice<[Int]> is drawable

rows.reason: It sorts the entries oldest first, with a URL tiebreak, and returns the URLs of the shortest run of oldest entries whose removal brings the total size within maxCacheSize. It returns [] when the cache already fits. The result is the evicted complement of a re-sorted list, mapped to URLs, so it is not a prefix or suffix of the input.
Sends an authorized GET /files request with path, page and limit query items, throws on a non-200 status, and decodes the server's file list. limit is a server-side page size for a network fetch.

It returns a CappedList whose shown is Array(collected.prefix(max(0, limit))): the longest leading run of at most limit elements, with negative limits clamped to 0. total is nil, and the wasTruncated flag is derived (shown.count >= limit). Quirk: the `end` argument is stored but ignored, so even `.trailing` gets the leading prefix, not a suffix.
rows.reread_note: public CappedList.stoppedEarly over [Element]; drawable with Element = Int. Its keeping: argument is recorded but never applied

rows.reason: It computes a line window: begin = max(startLine,1)-1 and end = min(begin + span, lineCount), with span clamped into 1...max(cap,1), plus an isTruncated flag. The window starts at an arbitrary offset rather than at the start of an input. It returns nil when the start is past the end of the file.

A limit <= 0 gives ("", !isEmpty), and a string whose utf8.count fits is returned whole with false. Otherwise it appends whole Characters while the running UTF-8 byte total stays <= limit and stops at the first that would not fit, returning true. So the result is the longest Character-aligned prefix within the byte budget, and the flag is accurate.
rows.reread_note: public String.prefix(utf8Bytes:), the motivating subject

rows.reason: It queries vec_beads for limit*3 nearest neighbours, filters them by project, and scores each by recency (now()), distance and pin bonus. It sorts by score and returns scored.prefix(limit). The capped list is computed from database I/O, not from an input sequence, and a negative limit traps in prefix.

It selects every bead_metadata row, keeps those for the project, sorts them newest first and returns Array(result.prefix(limit)). The list comes from a database read rather than from an input, and a negative limit traps.

This is a lint check. It returns [] unless braceDepth <= 0 and the line starts with a `var` declaration form without @MainActor, and in that case it returns one globalMutableWithoutIsolation violation whose detail is trimmed.prefix(80). braceDepth is a gate, not a size budget, so nothing in it is budgeted truncation.

It appends whole items while TokenEstimator's word-based estimate of the kept items joined by "\n\n" stays <= maxTokens, and breaks at the first item that would exceed. The estimate is monotone, so this is the longest leading run of items that fits. It returns nil when nothing fits: the first item is over budget or items is empty.
rows.reread_note: internal static leadingItems(_:fitting:) over [String]; returns nil when nothing fits

rows.reason: It keeps `previous` whole if its estimate is <= limit/2, then appends truncateToTokens(newest, remaining) joined with "\n". The result combines two inputs (the previous turn plus the head of newest), so it is not a prefix of either. It returns nil when neither part survives.

It converts the budget to maxWords = Int(maxTokens/1.33) and returns the text up to the start of word maxWords+1, with trailing whitespace stripped. Text with no more words is returned unchanged, and maxWords <= 0 gives "". The word count is the most whose estimate fits (checked for T < 200k), so FITS holds. But the cut is at a word boundary and the stripped whitespace, which costs 0 tokens, means it is not the longest fitting prefix.
rows.reread_note: private truncateToTokens(_:maxTokens:) over String; WEAK (word boundary); private, so no test target reaches it

rows.reason: It splits the content on "\n", finds the line containing the character offset, and returns up to 100 lines either side of it, joined. That is a window centred on an offset, not a prefix. An offset past the end leaves cursorLine at 0, so it returns the first 101 lines.

It filters policies into disabled and enabled groups, takes prefix(limit) of each, and formats them as a markdown string with a header and per-group headings. The output is generated text built from two filtered subsets, not a prefix of the input. A negative limit traps in prefix.

It walks results in rank order and keeps up to maxPerDocument per sourceFile until it has limit items, deferring the overflow. Then it fills any spare slots from the deferred items. Deferred items are appended after later-ranked ones, so the result is a re-ordered subset, not a contiguous prefix.

It strips the opening and closing fence lines of a code block and groups the remaining lines into pieces whose estimated tokens plus fence and heading overhead stay within maxTokens. It returns every piece, each re-fenced and prefixed with the heading, as RawChunks. That chunks the whole input rather than truncating it.

It splits the text on single spaces and emits overlapping windows of Int(maxTokens/1.33) words, stepping by window size minus overlap. It skips windows that are all whitespace and prefixes later windows with the heading. The result is a chunk list covering the whole input, not a truncation.

It runs a breadth-first traversal over the actor's in-memory edges for up to maxDepth hops from startId and collects every newly reached target node. maxDepth bounds hop count, not the size of an input. It reads mutable actor state, and a negative maxDepth traps on 0..<maxDepth.

It loads every SCIPSymbol node from the database, filters by a case-insensitive name match and an optional kind, and sorts exact matches first and then shorter names. It returns Array(results.prefix(limit)). This caps a computed search result, and a negative limit traps.

It runs a breadth-first traversal of SQLite graph_edges for up to maxDepth hops, querying the database per frontier node, and collects each newly reached target node's properties. maxDepth bounds hop count, not the size of an input. A negative maxDepth traps on 0..<maxDepth.

It ensures the schema exists, delegates to database.matchPath (a depth-limited BFS over leads_to edges, up to maxDepth hops) and decodes the rows into KGSkillNodes. The budget is traversal depth over the graph, not a size limit on an input.

It runs SQL `... WHERE skill_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?` with the limit and parses the rows. The cap is applied by the database to a query result, not to an input sequence. In SQLite a negative LIMIT means no limit.

It forwards query and maxResults as arguments to the remote DocumentationSearch MCP tool and returns its text fragments joined by "\n\n". Nothing is truncated locally. It returns nil when the tool is unavailable, errors, or returns no text.

It scans scalars while tracking bracket nesting from the starting depth, skipping over "..." string text. It returns the slice up to the bracket that brings depth to 0, or the whole text if none does. That is a delimiter-terminated prefix: depth is a nesting count, not a size budget.

It walks backwards from index while the preceding scalars are identifier characters and returns chars[start...index] as a String: the identifier ending at that index. index is a position to slice at, not a budget.

It parses leading digits and requires them to equal expectedOrdinal, followed by '.' or ')' and then whitespace. It returns the rest of the line with leading whitespace dropped, a suffix after a list marker, and returns nil on any mismatch. expectedOrdinal is a value to match, not a size budget.

Builds a new summary from the actor's fileSymbols state (a header line, then per-file path/symbol/import lines), stopping once an approximate word count (maxTokens/1.33) is reached. The check runs before a file's lines are added, so the output can overshoot the budget, and the header is always emitted. The result is generated text, not a prefix of any input.

Runs a SQL query with `LIMIT ?` bound to `limit`, then compactMaps the rows (dropping any without run_id) into FixtureHistoryRow values. It is a database fetch capped at the budget, not a truncation of an input sequence.

First replaces tabs with "→" (so even short results are not prefixes of the input), then returns the line unchanged if count <= max, otherwise String(visible.prefix(max)) + "…". The result is max+1 characters, and a negative max traps in prefix.

Groups positions by runSignature, then for each group with enough members applies the import, mass and identifier floors and calls nonOverlappingInstances to build RunClass values. `length` is the run length shared by the positions, not a budget. Output order follows Dictionary iteration, which varies between processes.

Walks the `length` items starting at `position` in lists[position.listId] and joins their Structure.appendSignature output (with consistent identifier renaming) into one signature string. It maps a window to a fingerprint and truncates nothing.

Maps each position to a RunInstance spanning `length` items, sorts the instances by range, and greedily keeps those that do not overlap the last kept instance in the same file. The result is a non-contiguous subset chosen by overlap, not a budget-sized prefix.

A lexer step. Starting at the inout `index`, it appends characters while each is a number, letter, '_' or a '.' followed by a digit, returns that numeric-literal token and advances `index` past it. The stopping point is a character-class predicate, not a size budget.
If value.count >= width it returns value unchanged (never truncates). Otherwise it appends spaces on the right up to `width` Characters, so despite the name it left-aligns.
If value.count >= width it returns value unchanged (never truncates). Otherwise it prepends spaces up to `width` Characters, which right-aligns the value.

It parses `source`, finds the innermost declaration covering `line` and collects its plain string literals that are non-empty and at most 40 characters. It dedupes them and returns `.prefix(16)` of that computed list. `line` is a locator, the cap is a fixed constant, and the capped list is not an input sequence.

It builds "  <template>:" + spaces + count + " (<tierBreakdown>)", with max(1, targetWidth - prefix.count - countStr.count) spaces to right-align the count at targetWidth. Nothing is truncated: an over-wide template still gets one space and its full text.
Generates exactly `count` fresh test Rule values with ids "\(prefix)_\(index)". `prefix` is an id string and nothing is truncated. A negative count traps on 0..<count.

Clamps the location to [0, length] and the range length to max(0, min(self.length, length - location)). When the location is out of bounds it moves the start (for a negative location it keeps the original length), so the result is not always a prefix of the original range. This is integer clamping, not truncation of a sequence.

Returns the content unchanged if content.count <= limit, otherwise String(content.prefix(limit)) + "…". The result is limit+1 characters and not a prefix of the input. A negative limit traps in prefix.
Sanitizes the query and delegates to runFTSQuery, which runs an FTS5 MATCH against the SQLite pool with `LIMIT ?` = limit. It is a capped database search, not a truncation of an input.
Sanitizes the tag and delegates to runFTSQuery, which runs a tag-column FTS5 MATCH with `LIMIT ?` = limit. It is a database search capped at the budget.
Sanitizes the query and delegates to runFTSQuery, which runs a title-column FTS5 MATCH with `LIMIT ?` = limit. It is a database search capped at the budget.

Returns [] for an empty query. Otherwise it runs SELECT ... snippet(...) ... WHERE col MATCH ? ORDER BY rank LIMIT ? on the DatabasePool and maps the rows to SearchResult. snippetTokens is passed to SQLite's snippet() and limit caps the fetched rows, so nothing in the input is truncated.

Returns self when maxCases >= count. Otherwise it rebuilds buckets taking min(bucket.count, room) per bucket until exactly maxCases cases are kept, so the result is the first min(maxCases, count) cases, contiguous from index 0, with the same build/describe closures. maxCases == 0 gives an empty enumeration. The original fullCount is carried, so isComplete reports truncation. A negative maxCases traps on a precondition instead of truncating.
rows.reread_note: public Enumeration.prefix(_:) counts cases; Enumeration carries build and describe closures, so no derived generator draws one

rows.reason: Runs a BFS over self.edges from the entry method, skipping visited nodes and any node at depth >= maxDepth, and appends every outgoing edge of each expanded node. maxDepth bounds the traversal depth, not the size of an input sequence. maxDepth <= 0 returns [].
Returns bytes.map { $0 ^ key }. `key` is an XOR operand, not a budget, and the output has the same length as the input.

Returns s if s.count <= limit, otherwise String(s.prefix(limit - 1)) + "…", which is exactly limit characters and not a prefix of s. limit <= 0 with a longer string traps on prefix(-1) (limit 0 with a non-empty s, or any negative limit).

Returns s if s.count <= limit, otherwise String(s.prefix(limit)) + "…", which is limit+1 characters (the seeded off-by-one bug), so even FITS fails. A negative limit with a non-empty s traps in prefix.
Always appends "…": s + "…" when s.count <= limit, otherwise String(s.prefix(limit - 1)) + "…". The result is never a prefix of s, and limit <= 0 with a longer s traps on prefix(-1).

Generates shrink candidates through Shrinkers.array (empty, the two halves, each drop-one array, element-simplified copies) and keeps those with count >= minimum. `minimum` is a floor on candidate length, not a cap, and the result is a list of candidate arrays.

Maps the text to alphabet indices and returns [] if any character falls outside the alphabet. Otherwise it returns shorten(codes, minimum: minimumLength, element: Shrinkers.integer) mapped back to strings: a list of shrink candidates at least minimumLength long, not a truncation.

Checks the precondition 0 <= index <= count, returns a mutable sub-span over [index, count), and sets the inout index to count. That is a slice from a position offset, with no size budget, and the function is mutating with an inout side effect.

Checks the precondition 0 <= index <= count, returns `extracting(last: count - index)` (the span from index to the end), and advances the inout index to count. It slices at an offset rather than fitting a budget.

Rope B-tree insertion. It mutates the child at `slot` through the body closure, recomputes the summary, and folds any spawned node back in through _applySpawn (merge or split), returning an optional overflow node. slot is a child index, not a budget.
Inserts an item into a rope leaf at `slot`, rebalancing undersized items and splitting the node when it is full. It returns the split-off node or nil. It mutates the tree and truncates nothing.
A factory that returns the enum case `.break(kind, size: size, newlines: .elective)`. size is stored as a payload, so there is no input sequence and no truncation.
Returns the diagnostic message "remove empty line(s) after '{'", choosing singular or plural by whether count > 1. count only picks the wording.
Copies the DateComponents and multiplies each non-nil scalable field (era, year, month, …, yearForWeekOfYear) by value. This is scalar arithmetic, not truncation.
Returns `.indexNode(index, self, depth: self.depth + 1)`, pushing an index key onto the coding-path linked list. It extends the path rather than truncating it.

Decimal multiplication. It throws on NaN, returns zero for zero-length operands, and otherwise computes the full-width product of the significands, which _assemble rounds to minExponent and the rounding mode. The `inexact` flag reports precision lost to rounding. This is numeric rounding, not a prefix of an input.
Delegates to _multiplyReportingInexact and drops the inexact flag, so it returns the rounded Decimal product. It is arithmetic and throws on NaN or overflow.

Delegates to _divideReportingInexact, which scales the dividend, takes a full-width quotient and rounds it through _assemble to minExponent. It returns only the quotient and throws on NaN or a zero divisor. This is numeric division.

If the exponent is already at or above minExponent it returns (self, false). Otherwise it divides the significand by 10^shift and rounds the quotient and remainder through _assemble with the rounding mode, returning an inexact flag. This is decimal rounding to a precision, not a prefix: the result may round up, and minExponent is an exponent, not a size budget.
Throws divideByZero when the divisor is 0. Otherwise it returns self with its significand replaced by the integer quotient significand / divisor, plus the UInt16 remainder. This is integer division.

Divides a progress fraction by an Int by multiplying the total by rhs. On overflow it simplifies first, and it falls back to an overflowed double fraction. It returns nil when lhs has no total or simplification fails. This is fraction arithmetic, not truncation.

Finds the first 0 byte at or after `index` in the readable bytes and decodes the bytes from `index` up to that terminator as UTF-8. It returns nil if `index` is outside readerIndex..<writerIndex or no terminator exists. `index` is a start offset, not a size budget, and nothing is cut to fit a limit.
Returns `[.formfeeds(count)]`, a one-piece Trivia that represents `count` form-feed characters. It is a constructor; `count` sets a repetition count rather than limiting any input.
Returns `[.newlines(count)]`, a one-piece Trivia for `count` newlines. It is a constructor with no input sequence to truncate.
Returns `[.spaces(count)]`, a one-piece Trivia for `count` spaces. It is a constructor that builds content of that size rather than cutting an input to fit.
Returns `[.tabs(count)]`, a one-piece Trivia for `count` tabs. It is a constructor with no truncation.

Builds a profile path of stacks+2 points, after clamping stacks to at least 1 and radius to at least scaleLimit/2, and lathes it into a cone Mesh with `slices` and `poleDetail ?? 3`. It is geometry generation. Purity depends on the caller-supplied isCancelled closure.
Copies `self`, sets `polygon.id = id` and returns the copy. It is a field setter, not a truncation.

Reads back a rendered GPU texture, computes statistics, a colour probe and a histogram with `bins` bins (on CPU or GPU), and renders a histogram preview texture `histogramHeight` tall. This is image analysis with GPU/texture I/O; bins and height are resolution parameters, not budgets on an input sequence.
Builds a MaskShapeRecipe of kind `.regularPolygon`, with sides clamped to max(sides, 3) and feather clamped to [0, 1]. It is a value constructor with parameter clamping; no input is truncated.

Traps on a negative count and returns [] for count 0. Otherwise _minImplementation keeps a sorted buffer of the `count` smallest elements seen during a full scan. The result is the k smallest elements sorted by the predicate, a selection that is not a contiguous prefix of the input. It is pure as long as the predicate is.
Returns `.init(name: "low", value: value.description)`, an HTML attribute factory. The Int is rendered as the attribute value and nothing is truncated.
Returns `.init(name: "min", value: value.description)`, an HTML attribute factory with no truncation.
Returns `.init(name: "tabindex", value: value.description)`, an HTML attribute factory. The Int is serialized, not used as a budget.

Computes x raised to the integer power n with libm_pow. When n is not exactly representable as a Double, it splits n into high and low parts rounded toward zero and multiplies the two powers. This is numeric exponentiation with no input sequence.
Returns the n-th root of x: NaN for a negative x with even n, cbrtf when n == 3, and otherwise signOf(x) * powf(|x|, 1/n). This is plain numeric computation; n is a degree, not a budget.
Returns `.init(core: .nop)` and ignores the `context` parameter entirely. It builds a no-op io_uring request value.

Returns `.init(core: .readUnregisteredSlot(file:buffer:offset:context:))`, building a read-request descriptor. No I/O happens at construction; offset is a file position and context a user tag, so nothing is truncated.

Runs a sqlite-vec k-NN query (`k = topK`, or over-fetches topK*3 and adds `LIMIT topK` when sourceTypes is non-empty) and maps the rows to SearchResults. topK caps a list fetched from the database. It does not truncate an input sequence, and the function does I/O.

Builds a CloneReportJSON.CrossReport struct (tool, version, mode, fileCount, duplicated-line count, clone count, mapped clones) and encodes it to a JSON string. fileCount is only copied into a field. Nothing is truncated.

Groups findings by rule and then by file, builds sorted RuleImpact and FileImpact records, and passes `filesChecked` through, falling back to the count of distinct affected files. This is aggregation and ranking; nothing is truncated against `filesChecked`.
Copies self and overwrites score, tier, whySuggested and whyMightBeWrong where the argument is non-nil. It is a copy-with-override builder. score is a replacement value, not a budget.

Returns nil unless the line's count of leading spaces equals `expectedIndent` exactly. Otherwise it returns the trimmed text before the first colon, or nil for list items, lines with no colon and empty keys. `expectedIndent` is an equality filter for YAML parsing, not a size budget.
A deprecated factory whose body is just `.custom(trials: trials)`. It wraps the count in an enum case and truncates nothing.

Binary-searches buckets sorted by `start` for the last bucket whose start is <= index. It returns that bucket if its `indices` contain `index`, and nil for an empty array or an index outside it. It is a lookup of one element, not a truncation; a capped loop precondition traps only if the search fails to converge.

Splits values into those below the pivot and those at or above it. It then returns arrays made by repeating each group's first element group-count times, along with below.count; if either group is empty it returns (values, 0). The pivot is a comparison value, not a size budget, and the output is deliberately not a prefix or a permutation.
Returns `values + [value]`, which appends the int. It makes the array longer, so it never truncates.
